features.title: Training Hub home
features.what: This is your dashboard and the manual for the hub: your next steps, the feature checklist and the leaderboards.
features.how: Start with the checklist, then jump into Think, Theory or Trim from the menu at the top.
features.why: Every module trains one habit, MSPC: Move, Specifics, Priorities, Calculation. It replaces chaotic thinking with a routine.
features.ranks: Your XP level and rank sit in the top bar. Content runs from Free to Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced and Master.

features.title: Think: MSPC trainer
features.what: The MSPC trainer drills the four questions you ask before every move, on positions where the answer is positional, not only tactical.
features.how: Read the position, then answer Move, Specifics, Priorities and Calculation in that order. Check the feedback before the next one.
features.why: Most blunders come from skipping one of the four questions. Asking them in order turns it into a habit that runs in your games.
features.ranks: Each difficulty level has a free sample set. Your Think rank grows with accuracy and streaks.

features.title: Shuffle Trainer
features.what: Shuffle serves random MSPC positions one after another, so you practise without knowing what comes next.
features.how: Pick a scope, play the position, then move straight on to the next one. Ranked Shuffle counts towards your rating.
features.why: In a real game nobody tells you which theme is coming. Random order trains you to recognise the theme yourself.
features.ranks: The filters follow the five levels. Ranked runs feed your accuracy and the leaderboard.

features.title: Bot Deep-Thinking Trainer
features.what: You play a Stockfish bot at a strength you choose, starting around 300 ELO, and run MSPC on your moves.
features.how: Play on the board. After an inaccuracy or a blunder the game pauses and asks for your MSPC. You can always continue with the mistake and see how it is punished.
features.why: Deep thinking on every move is the skill. If you doubt a move, you have not thought about it long enough yet.
features.ranks: Playing the local engine is free. Paid tiers add live Socratic feedback from the coach.

features.title: Board Vision and Fundamentals
features.what: Quick drills for the basics: board coordinates, knight paths and legal moves.
features.how: Choose a drill and play it against the clock. Flip the board orientation to practise both colours.
features.why: Fast, accurate board vision frees your attention for the Specifics step of MSPC.
features.ranks: These drills are for every level. Faster and cleaner is the goal.

features.title: Survival and Defense Challenges
features.what: Challenges against Stockfish where you either hold a worse position or convert a winning one.
features.how: Pick a challenge and survive the number of moves it asks for, or finish the conversion without letting the win slip.
features.why: Defending and converting are separate skills, and both decide how many points you keep.
features.ranks: Challenges get harder as you move up the five levels.

features.title: Puzzles by theme
features.what: Practice puzzles by tactical theme, such as forks, pins, back rank mates and endgames. Nothing here changes your rating.
features.how: Choose a theme, use Learn to see the idea, then drill a short set. Missed puzzles go to your Mistake Deck.
features.why: Seeing one pattern many times builds recognition, and recognition saves you calculation in step C of MSPC.
features.ranks: These puzzles are unrated, so you can experiment freely. Rated puzzles live under Ranked.

features.title: Openings
features.what: The opening trainer teaches full repertoires: Caro-Kann, Colle-Koltanowski and the Semi-Slav, with Learn and Drill modes.
features.how: Learn a line first, then drill it. If you play another move that is in the chapter tree, the trainer follows that branch instead of calling it wrong.
features.why: MSPC puzzles appear only at critical moments, so you learn why a move is played, not just which one.
features.ranks: Level 1 is free for everyone. Levels 2 to 5 need a paid plan or token. Each level adds deeper lines on top of the earlier ones.

features.title: Middlegame

features.why: A plan starts with Specifics: pawn structure, weak squares, piece activity and king safety.
features.ranks: Five tiers from Free to Master. Free covers basic lessons and puzzles, and the deeper sections unlock with higher levels.

features.title: Trim: game review
features.what: Trim reviews your own game with Stockfish and finds the exact moves where your rating leaks.
features.how: Paste a PGN or import your game, then go through the mistakes one at a time. Answer M, S, P and C yourself before you see the better move.
features.why: You learn most from your own mistakes, and MSPC shows which step failed: the threat, the position, the forcing moves or the calculation.
features.ranks: A new member's first Trim is free. After that a review uses a token. Reviews also feed your severity meter and working points.
